atoms.b: The most common punctuation mark used to separate parenthetical clauses is the ((++comma colon)).
Use commas to introduce ((++non-essential essential)) information that is closely related to the main idea. This information could be a description, clarification or just added detail.

instruction.text: If the sentence below contains non-essential information, separate the non-essential portion of the sentence with one or more commas. In some of these sentences, no comma is needed.

instruction.text: If the sentence below contains non-essential information, separate the non-essential portion of the sentence with one or more commas. In some of these sentences, no comma is needed.

The student who loves flying down the halls on her big wheels is thrilled to be back in school. ((--,))

feedback.finish: Notice that, unlike in the previous sentence, the student isn’t referred to by name here.
